NUCLEOSIDES & NUCLEOTIDES, 14(3-5), 337-340 (1995) 
SYNTHESIS OF 9-(2-HYDROXYETHOXYMETHYL)GUANINE 
(ACYCLOVIR) FROM GUANOSINE 
Hiroshi Shiragami, Yoshihito Koguchi, Yasuhiro Tanaka, Satoshi Takamatsu, 
Yumiko Uchida, Takashi Ineyama and Kunisuke Izawa* 
Central Research Laboratories, Ajinomoto Co., Inc. 
1-1 Suzuki-cho, Kawasaki-ku, Kawasaki 210, Japan 
Abstract: A convenient synthesis of 9-(2-hydroxyethoxymethyl)guanine (acyclovir) from 
guanosine by chemical transpurination was developed. The isomerization of the 7-isomer 
to the desired 9-isomer and the purification of the 9-isomer was achieved simply by 
concentration, heating and further crystallization. 
Introduction 
The discovery of 9-(2-hydroxyethoxymethyl)guanine (acyclovir)la-c (1) which has 
potent activity against herpes simplex type 1 and 2 viruses triggered a world wide effort to 
synthesize guanine nucleosides and acyclic nucleoside analogues.2a-f Several methods for 
the synthesis of acyclovir have been reported. Previously, Boryski and Golankiewicz 
reported3 transpurination of tetraa~etylguanosine~ 
(6), leading to 9- and 7-(2- 
acetoxyethoxymethyl)-N2-acetyIguanine (5). However, many problems occur when 
adapting this method for large-scale production, because it requires many steps and 
isolation of intermediary products, and has less regioselectivity. 
Here, we wish to report more convenient and economical synthesis of acyclovir (1) 
from natural g uanos i tie (2) by c hem ical t ran spu ri nat ion. 
Results and Disciission 
Reacting 1,3-dioxolane (3) with acetic anhydride in the presence of acid catalyst 
gave (2-acetoxyethoxy)methyl acetate5 (4). The transpurination reaction of guanosine (2) 
with this acyclic sugar moiety 4 in the presence of acetic anhydride and catalytic amount of 
acid gave a mixture of 9-(2-acetoxyethoxyrnethyl)-N~-acetylguanine 
(5a) and 742- 
acetoxyethoxymethyl)-N2-acetylguanine (5b) in high yield (FIG. I). Various acid catalysts 
were applicable to the transpurination, as summarized in TABLE 1. The reaction proceeded 
with or without solvent.

solvents.name: none / neat (reaction proceeded with or without solvent; MeCN or DMF also used in Table 1)

conditions.other: Catalyst for making 4 can be the same as that used in transpurination, enabling a one-pot process with guanosine

steps.notes: General procedure only (ref. 5); no isolated amounts reported. Table 1 shows one-pot reaction of guanosine with 1,3-dioxolane and Ac2O gave similar results to the two-step route.
steps.evidence: Reacting 1,3-dioxolane (3) with acetic anhydride in the presence of acid catalyst gave (2-acetoxyethoxy)methyl acetate (4).

steps.step_label: Experimental: transpurination of guanosine with 4 → mixture of 9-isomer (5a) and 7-isomer (5b)

solvents.name: none (neat, acetic anhydride serves as medium)

conditions.other: HPLC showed tetraacetylguanosine (6) forms first, then converts to 5; transpurination of guanosine does not occur without acetic anhydride; 9/7-isomer ratio ca. 1.45 after transpurination

steps.notes: Various acid catalysts applicable (p-TsOH·H2O, H2SO4, sulfanilic acid, H3PO4); solvent optional (MeCN 82 °C, DMF 120 °C)
steps.evidence: To 50 g (176.5 mmol) of guanosine were added 62 g (353 mmol) of 4, 180 g (1.75 mol) of acetic anhydride and 3.4 g (17.5 mmol) of p-toluenesulfonic acid monohydrate, and the mixture was stirred at 100 °C for 20 h.

steps.step_label: Concentration and thermal isomerization of 7-isomer (5b) to 9-isomer (5a)

conditions.other: Volatile components distilled off, then residue heated under reduced pressure; conditions milder than previously reported (230 °C, 5 min)

steps.notes: Isomerization achieved simply by concentration and heating under reduced pressure
steps.evidence: The reaction mixture was concentrated under reduced pressure (10 mmHg) at 50 °C for 1 h. The resulting residue was stirred at 100 °C under reduced pressure (10 mmHg) for 20 h.

conditions.other: Crystals filtered, washed with ethyl acetate (20 mL), dried under reduced pressure; alternative crystallization solvents: acetonitrile or water; 9/7 ratio after crystallization 120

steps.notes: Purity determined by HPLC; 5a crystallizes selectively from the concentrate
steps.evidence: The crude crystals (53 g) contained 46.9 g of 5a (86% yield), accompanied with 270 mg (0.5%) of 5b, which were determined by HPLC.

steps.step_label: Deacetylation with aqueous NaOH and neutralization with HCl → acyclovir (1)

conditions.other: Neutralized with 1 M HCl; precipitate collected by filtration

steps.evidence: 10 g of crude crystals containing 5a were dissolved in 100 mL of 5% aqueous NaOH ... neutralized by 1M HCl and the resulting precipitate was filtered to provide 6.4 g of 1 (92% yield)
